## [CN]规则
## [EN]Rules

| 中文 | English |
|:---|:---|
| 见右列。 | **Language version**: Swift 5.9 syntax that builds with the Swift 6 toolchain of Xcode 27; minimum deployment target as in the podspec (iOS 13 for the library). Gate newer APIs with `if #available` / `@available`, never with OS version strings. |
| | **Objective-C compatibility of the library**: public types inherit from `NSObject` (or a UIKit class) and are `@objc(CYLName)` with the old Objective-C name; members that Objective-C callers use are `@objc(oldSelector:)` so the selector does not change. Keep `CYL` prefixes on Objective-C names and `cyl_` on category members (Swift extensions of UIKit types keep `@objc(cyl_name)`). Do not rename public API; add a new name and deprecate the old one when a rename is needed. |
| | **Keep the Swift names callers already use**: Clang imported every Objective-C method into Swift under a name, often shortened (it drops a trailing word that repeats the return or parameter type: `-cyl_getViewControllerInsteadOfNavigationController` is `cyl_getViewControllerInsteadOfNavigation()` in Swift), or set by `NS_SWIFT_NAME`. A translated member keeps that Swift name and the old selector: `@objc(cyl_getViewControllerInsteadOfNavigationController) public func cyl_getViewControllerInsteadOfNavigation()`. Check the name in the generated Swift interface of the old header or in Swift callers (`grep` the examples) before translating. |
| | **Kept names and SonarCloud** (added 2026-11-12): names that must stay for compatibility (`cyl_` category members, `CYL` C functions and constants with their Objective-C names) break SonarCloud's Swift naming rules `swift:S100` / `swift:S115`. SonarCloud's Swift analyzer does not support `// NOSONAR`, and automatic analysis ignores `sonar.issue.ignore.*`, so these findings are marked **Accept** in the SonarCloud UI by the maintainer (bulk change, filtered by rule and file). Never accept a name that is free to change: private and internal helpers, and the Swift-side names of `@_cdecl` entry points, use lowerCamelCase (`cylImageNamedEntryPoint`).
| | **Names**: Swift API Design Guidelines: clarity at the point of use, argument labels that read as phrases, `is`/`has` for Booleans, no abbreviations except well-known ones (`URL`, `ID`). Types are `UpperCamelCase`, everything else `lowerCamelCase`. |
| | **Types**: `let` by default; value types for data that has no identity; `final` for classes that are not meant to be subclassed (not for public classes that apps subclass, such as `CYLPlusButton`). Prefer `guard` for early exits; no force unwrapping (`!`) or `try!` in library code, except for `IBOutlet`-style invariants documented in a comment. |
| | **Associated objects** (state of category-style extensions): one private `static var` key per value (`UInt8` address), accessed through `objc_getAssociatedObject` / `objc_setAssociatedObject` in a computed property. |
| | **Concurrency**: UI code is `@MainActor`; library entry points used from Objective-C stay synchronous on the main thread as before. No unstructured `Task` in the library without a comment that says who cancels it. |
| | **Errors**: Swift `throws` for new Swift-only API; `NSError **` style (`throws` exposed to Objective-C) where an Objective-C method returned `NSError`. |
| | **Comments**: every public declaration has a documentation comment in the three-line `/** … */` block form (`/**`, ` * [EN] …`, ` * [CN] …`, ` */`), bilingual as the rest of the library ([Public API comment format] in `AGENTS.md`); no `///` in library files. `// FIX: issue #N` notes move with the code they explain. |
| | **Formatting**: 4 spaces, lines up to 120 characters, one type per file named after it (extensions: `UIView+CYLName.swift`), `// MARK: -` sections, trailing closures only for the last closure argument. |
| | **Translation from Objective-C**: keep behavior identical (including nil handling of the old code and the order of side effects); translate tests' expectations, not the tests themselves; one file per commit when a file is large, each commit with a clean build, the unit tests and the migration score. |
